content.text: Based on your gist, it appears that you are using the "FileSystemBinaryStore", likely from a configuration such as:
-Dfcrepo.modeshape.configuration=classpath:config/minimal-default/repository.json
The first thing I would suggest it to instead use a MySQL or PostgreSQL backend object store.
See 4.6:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA46/Configuring+JDBC+Object+Store
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA47/Configuring+JDBC+Object+Store
Secondly, if this is a new repository, I would highly suggest you start with Fedora 4.7.0.
Additionally, can you describe the nature of the "bulk import"? Do you have control over the number of concurrent import clients?
Andrew, thank you for the quick response.
The bulk import is for sufia 6.x to 7.x migration; currently in progress at
https://github.com/projecthydra/sufia/tree/7.2-migration
. It's a single client / straightforward script creating each object and pulling its content from one fedora to another.
, I have just checked my logs and I'm seeing the same error using 4.7.0 with metadata in PostgreSQL and binaries on a CIFS-mounted network share.  My config is at:
https://gist.github.com/escowles/5b9f19548c32148f5a908293636499a3

I just did a quick check of the MODE BOM and tagged source for 5.1.0.Final and 5.2.0.Final, I don't see anything that makes sense for a SocketTimeoutException. On older versions of MODE there is some temp file activity around that line number, but they shouldn't be in play.
I agree,
. It appears that the ModeShape/FileSystemBinaryStore code that could potentially throw that error is in ModeShape release 4.5.0.Final:
https://github.com/ModeShape/modeshape/blob/modeshape-4.5.0.Final/modeshape-jcr/src/main/java/org/modeshape/jcr/value/binary/FileSystemBinaryStore.java#L129
...which was last included in Fedora 4.6.0.
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/fcrepo-4.6.0/pom.xml#L47
That leaves me to wonder how the error can be coming from a Fedora 4.7.0??
Doing this import in 100-object chunks seems to help. I'm now nearing 500 objects and haven't had this error.
That is good to hear,

. I am still curious as to what is going on since you are supposedly ingesting into a Fedora 4.7.0... but the version of the FileSystemBinaryStore class does not correspond to the version of ModeShape that is released with Fedora 4.7.0.
I'm still importing into the 4.6.0; we're working on getting 4.7/postgres set up to try it there. Will update! Esme has said he experienced the same error on 4.7.
Do you have any updates,
? I believe all investigation of this issue are waiting on that.
We haven't been able to replicate on 4.7. I'd be fine closing this except that Esme said he's seen the same error on 4.7 so I'll defer to him!
I saw the error with 4.7.0 — the stacktrace I saw was very slightly different from the one in
https://gist.github.com/hackmastera/a4432aded8790482c2e7e544228c4232
(a couple of the line numbers are different):
org.modeshape.jcr.value.binary.BinaryStoreException: java.net.SocketTimeoutException
at org.modeshape.jcr.value.binary.FileSystemBinaryStore.storeValue(FileSystemBinaryStore.java:128)
at org.modeshape.jcr.value.binary.AbstractBinaryStore.storeValue(AbstractBinaryStore.java:251)
at org.modeshape.jcr.value.binary.BinaryStoreValueFactory.create(BinaryStoreValueFactory.java:257)
at org.modeshape.jcr.value.binary.BinaryStoreValueFactory.create(BinaryStoreValueFactory.java:49)
at org.modeshape.jcr.JcrValueFactory.createBinary(JcrValueFactory.java:149)
at org.modeshape.jcr.JcrValueFactory.createBinary(JcrValueFactory.java:41)
at org.fcrepo.kernel.modeshape.FedoraBinaryImpl.setContent(FedoraBinaryImpl.java:180)
at org.fcrepo.http.api.ContentExposingResource.replaceResourceBinaryWithStream(ContentExposingResource.java:608)
at org.fcrepo.http.api.FedoraLdp.createOrReplaceObjectRdf(FedoraLdp.java:358)
at sun.reflect.GeneratedMethodAccessor53.invoke(Unknown Source)
I was doing a long-running ingest operation using Plum/CurationConcerns/Hydra and the Fedora 4.7.0 release, and my repository configuration is here:
https://gist.github.com/escowles/5b9f19548c32148f5a908293636499a3
— the disk in question is a CIFS-mounted Isilon storage cluster.
I may have preemptively bumped down the priority; if it needs to go back up of course please do so
Thanks
, would you please update your comment above to add your scenario details:
What are you actually doing
What versions of Fedora are in play
What configuration of Fedora is in use
Since this is a "binary store" error, what is the architecture of you binary storage file system?

, I've updated my comment with more info about my setup.  I plan to spend some time next week looking at Fedora performance during ingest.  In addition to this error, I've also seen performance gradually slow down over time.  Restarting Fedora periodically seems to fix this, but I'm hoping that profiling Fedora will help discover why it's happening.
We are seeing a similar error on Fcrepo 4.7.1 when uploading a single large file (~2GB) - see [
stacktrace
I would think this issue could be resolved by configuring the HTTP connection timeout.
It may make sense to adjust your servlet container's socket_timeout:
https://tomcat.apache.org/connectors-doc/common_howto/timeouts.html
Greetings all, this ticket is a year old, but I've recently encountered behavior that seems to be related to this bug within versions 4.7.2 and 4.7.5.

I've had this error crop up infrequently and intermittently on three separate environments. The files being processed when encountering the error are < 10MB. Two of the environments have application services spread across four machines. One environment has all services on the same machine, except for the mariadb service supporting the modeshape database which is on a different machine.
Here's a [
stacktrace
] and [
repository.json
] for reference.

, I saw your link for configuring the httpd connection timeout, but it looks like the documentation is specifically for using AJP/mod_jk (which we are not). If you (or anyone else) happens to have any other tips, hints, or suggestions for alleviating this issue, it'd be greatly appreciated!
did you find any solution to this issue? We're running into it at Oxford and, like you, we're not using mod_jk
is there any other way to resolve the HTTP connection timeout?
I'm closing this issue as part of a jira repository scrubbing.  It appears to be out of date, no longer applicable, or addressed by future versions of Fedora.
Bulk importing objects into Sufia 7.2-based application. Erroring between 100 and 300 objects. See gist for stack trace:
https://gist.github.com/hackmastera/a4432aded8790482c2e7e544228c4232
